532.t: Moving from studio work to leading his own groups
532.s: Watts says recording his own music was natural; his focus was always jazz, and he kept a quartet at Donte's through the studio years.
532.q: Well for me it was all part of a natural process. The music that I grew up listening to and the reason why I wanted to play music and the reason why I started playing was the music of the groups of Miles Davis, John Coltrane, all of the sidemen that played with Miles that became such great leaders,…

229.t: South Frisco Jazz Band and Club New Orleans
229.s: He plays weekends in Huntington Beach with the white South Frisco Jazz Band, opening at Club New Orleans on election night 1972.
229.ch: The Legends of Jazz and life on the road
229.q: During that time I was working with a white band from Huntington Beach, called the South Frisco Jazz Band and I worked out there six months with them just weekends.

388.t: Roosevelt Grill house band with Jack Lesberg
388.s: At Gibson's Roosevelt Grill, Leeman and Lesberg are the house rhythm section behind Joe Venuti, Buck Clayton and Peanuts Hucko, and later back Bobby Hackett.
388.q: years, that I just can't put my finger on many of them without research. Until we came to the point of Dick Gibson, and his World's Greatest Jazz Band, and he opened into the Roosevelt Grill in New York, and had a music policy there. That's another one of his wonderful promotions for jazz music.
